Physics

courses.label: PHYS 001
courses.title: Pre-University Physics
paras: This course covers the topics in Ontario Year 3 to 5 essential for first year university physics. The course includes mechanics, gravitation, vibrations and waves, heat, electricity, light and optics.
Successful completion of this course fulfills the University admission requirements where high school Physics is necessary.
No University Credit.

courses.label: PHYS 010
courses.title: Physics Seminar
paras: This seminar brings together Honours Physics (including Co-op students) in Years 2,3 and 4, to receive information concerning the activities of the Physics Department and to hear invited speakers.
Course Descriptions Physics

courses.label: PHYS 011
courses.title: Mechanics
paras: Brief review of kinematics. Particle dynamics, work, energy, conservation of energy. Conservation of linear momentum, collisions. Rotational kinematics and dynamics, conservation of angular momentum. Equilibrium of rigid bodies. Oscillation and waves. For students in Year 1 Engineering.

courses.label: PHYS 103
courses.title: Mechanics in Human Movement
paras: An introduction to the physical principles required for the analysis of the mechanics of human movement. A course for Kinesiology students. Lab alternate weeks, optional tut.
Note Normally students who have completed Ontario Year 5 Phys should select Phys 104 instead of 103.

courses.label: PHYS 104
courses.title: Mechanics in Human Movement
paras: An introduction to the physical principles required for the analysis of the mechanics of human movement. A course for Kinesiology students. Prereq: Ontario Year 5 Phys Lab alternate weeks, optional! tut.

courses.label: PHYS 105
courses.title: Electrical Science
paras: Basic electricity, magnetism and electronics. An introduction to the physical principles required for an understanding of the electrical instruments used in Kinesiology. A course for Kinesiology students. Prereg: Phys 103 or 104. Lab alternate weeks, optional tut.

courses.label: PHYS 111
courses.title: Physics For the Life Sciences 1
paras: An introduction to physics for students intending to concentrate their further studies in biology, medicine or dentistry; includes particle kinematics and dynamics, energy and momentum conservation, gravitation, rotational mechanics, fluid mechanics, elasticity and oscillations.
Phys 1171L F 3L 0.25 Physics For The Life Sciences 1 Laboratory For students taking Phys 111. Lab a/ternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 112
courses.title: Physics For The Life Sciences 2
paras: A continuation of Phys 111; includes wave motion, normal modes of vibration, sound, hearing, temperature, heat, kinetic theory of gases, thermodynamics, electrostatic force and potential, electric current and power, DC circuits, magnetic fields and induction.

courses.label: PHYS 112L
courses.title: Physics For The Life Sciences 2 Laboratory
paras: For students taking Phys 112. Lab alternative weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 121
courses.title: Introductory Physics 1
paras: An introductory course in physics for students intending to concentrate their future studies in the physical sciences, optometry or mathematics; includes particle kinematics and dynamics, forces in nature, work and energy, Conservation of energy and linear momentum..
Prereq: Ontario Year 5 Math-Functions and Relations, and Calculus. Ontario Year 5 Physics recommended, Science students must take 127L with this course..

courses.label: PHYS 121L
courses.title: Introductory Physics 1 Laboratory
paras: For students taking Phys 121. Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 122
courses.title: Introductory Physics 2
paras: This course is a continuation of Phys 121; includes rotational kinematics and dynamics, conservation of angular momentum, osciiiating systems, gravitation, electrical currents and resistive circuits, capacitative and inductive circuits, alternating currents and resonant circuits.
Prereq: Phys 121. Science students must take 122L with this course.

courses.label: PHYS 122L
courses.title: Introductory Physics 2 Laboratory
paras: For students taking Phys 122.
Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 162L

courses.label: PHYS 163

paras: This course is a continuation of Phys 162; includes topics listed in the description of Phys 122 plus enrichment topics, e.g. Fourier series, complex exponentials.
Prereq: Phys 162. Science students must take 163L with this course.

courses.label: PHYS 163L
courses.title: Enriched Introductory Physics 2 Laboratory
paras: For students taking Phys 163.
Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 222
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism 1
paras: Coulomb’s law, electric field, Gauss’ law, potential, capacitance, properties of dielectrics, current, resistance, electromotive force, D.C. circuits and instruments.
Prereq: First year phys and catculus. Not for Hons. Phys students. Phys Majors must take 222L with this course.

courses.label: PHYS 222L
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism 1 Laboratory
paras: For students taking Phys 222.
Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 223
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism 2
paras: Magnetic fields, induced electromotive forces, magnetic properties of matter, alternating currents, electromagnetic waves.
Prereq: Phys 222. Not for Hons. Phys students. Phys Majors must take 223L with this course.

courses.label: PHYS 223L
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism 2 Laboratory
paras: For students taking Phys 223.
Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 226
courses.title: Optics 1
paras: Reflection and refraction at plane and curved surfaces, thin and thick lenses, optical instruments. Prereq: First year phys and calculus. Not for Hons. Phys students. Phys Majors must take Phys 226L with this course.

courses.label: PHYS 226L
courses.title: Optics 1 Laboratory
paras: For students taking Phys 226. Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 227
courses.title: Optics 2
paras: The wave nature of light, interference, diffraction, slits and gratings, resolution, polarization, photometry, colour.
Prereq: Phys 226. Not for Hons. Phys students. Phys Majors must take Phys 227L with this course.

courses.label: PHYS 227L
courses.title: Optics 2 Laboratory
paras: For students taking Phys 227. Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 243
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism
paras: Electric & Magnetic Fields, Capacitance & dielectrics, electromagnetic induction, instruments, Magnetic properties of matter. : Prereq: First year phys and calculus. This course is primarily intended for Hons. Chem students.

courses.label: PHYS 243L
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism Laboratory
paras: For students taking Phys 243. ‘ Lab. alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 244A
courses.title: Quantum Physics 1
paras: Electronic charge, special relativity, particle accelerators, black body radiation and Planck’s law, photoelectric effect. Bohr atom, wave equation, eigenfunctions and eigenvalues, wave properties of light, x-ray production and properties, Compton effect, de Broglie’s hypothesis, Heisenberg’s - uncertainty principle.
Prereq: A first year phys course and Math 113 or equivalent.

courses.label: PHYS 244B
courses.title: Quantum Physics 2
paras: Schrodinger equation, wave functions, potential steps barriers and wells, transmission and reflection probabilities, tunnel effect, Hydrogen atom, Zeeman effect, selection rules, electron spin and the Pauli exclusion principle, relativistic Doppler effect, elementary statistical mechanics, basic crystallography.
Prereq: Phys 244A or equivalent.
Course Descriptions Physics

courses.label: PHYS 246
courses.title: Physical Optics
paras: Nature of light, wave motion, superposition of waves. Interference of light, Fraunhofer diffraction and resolution timit of optical instruments; the diffraction grating and the analysis of light. Fresnel diffraction. Potarized light. Coherence of light, lasers, holography. Fibre Optics.
Prereq: First year phys and calculus. Coreg: Phys 246L. This course is primarily intended for students registered in the Optom programme.

courses.label: PHYS 246L
courses.title: Physical Optics Laboratory
paras: For students taking Phys 246. Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 250
courses.title: The Solar System
paras: An introduction to the astronomy and astrophysics
of the solar system for students with a background in (elementary) University Physics and Mathematics. Prereq: First year Phys and Math.

courses.label: PHYS 251
courses.title: The Stellar System
paras: An introduction to the astronomy and astrophysics of objects beyond the solar system for students with a background in (elementary) University Physics and Mathematics.
Prereq: First year Phys and Math.

courses.label: PHYS 253
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism
paras: An introductory course in electricity and magnetism; includes Coulomb’s Law, electric fields, Gauss’ Law, electric potential, capacitance and dielectrics, magnetic forces and fields, inductance, magnetization, Maxwell’s equations, electromagnetic waves.

Prereq: First year phys and calculus, Math 2176. Physics majors must take 253L with this course. Recommended for students in Honours programmes. This course forms a basis for the understanding of most of today’s electronic and electrical technology.

courses.label: PHYS 253L
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism Laboratory
paras: For students taking Phys 253.
Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 254
courses.title: Thermal Physics and Properties of Matter
paras: An introductory course in properties of matter, kinetic theory and heat; includes elasticity, fluid mechanics, viscosity, diffusion, kinetic theory of gases, transport properties, termperature and heat, thermodynamics, heat engines.
Prereq: First year phys and calculus. Recommended for students in Honours programmes.

courses.label: PHYS 255
courses.title: Quantum Physics
paras: Background to quantum physics: special relativity, Bohr atom, wave-particle properties, uncertainty and wave packets. Introduction to quantum mechanics: equation for travelling wave, Schrédinger equation, solutions with potentials, correspondence principle, brief description of transitions and radiation processes.
Prereq: First year phys and calculus. Recommended for students in Hons. programmes.

courses.label: PHYS 256
courses.title: Wave Motion and Optics
paras: An introductory course in wave motion and optics; includes wave functions, the wave equation and wave speeds, superposition, energy density, standing waves, Fourier analysis, modulation and detection, Doppler shift, interference, diffraction, resolution of optical instruments, polarization. Prereq: First year phys and calculus. Physics majors must take 256L with this course. Recommended for students in Honours programmes.

courses.label: PHYS 256L
courses.title: Optics Laboratory
paras: For students taking Phys 256. Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 259
courses.title: Crystallography and X-Ray Diffraction
paras: Space lattices, symmetry, crystal structure, crystal geometry and stereographic projections. Electronic structure of atoms and atomic bonding in solids. Theory of X-ray diffraction, X-ray methods and the reciprocal lattice. Crystal formation, crystal defects and physical properties of crystals.
Prereq: First year phys and calculus. Coreq: Phys 259L

courses.label: PHYS 259L
courses.title: Crystallography and X-Ray Diffraction Laboratory
paras: For students taking Phys 259.
Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 270
courses.title: Laboratory
paras: Further experiments in optics and properties of matter, for students taking Phys 256L.
Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 271
courses.title: Laboratory
paras: Further experiments in electricity, magnetism and properties of matter, for students taking Phys 253L.
Course Descriptions 421 Physics

courses.label: PHYS 301
courses.title: Physical Techniques for Biologists 1
paras: Visible, UV, dark field, phase, interference, polarizing and fluorescence microscopy; electron microscopy; visible and UV spectroscopy; polarography; pH and ion electrodes; osmometers; densitometers; radioactive tracers and counters; introductory electronics; data analysis.
Prereq: First year phys. Physics students may not take this course for credit.

courses.label: PHYS 302
courses.title: Physicat Techniques for Biologists 2
paras: infrared, Roman and fluorescence spectroscopy; nuclear magnetic and electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy; optical rotary dispersion and circular dichroism; X-ray diffraction; chromatography and electrophoresis; differential scanning calorimetry; ultra centrifugation; flame photometry; X-ray and atomic absorption spectroscopy; cell counting, cytofluorometry and cell viabitity.
Prereq: First year physics. Physics students may not take this course for credit.

courses.label: PHYS 324
courses.title: Atomic and Nuclear Physics 1
paras: Fundamentals of modern physics, special theory of relativity, quantization of electromagnetic radiation, wave properties of particles, the hydrogen atom. Prereq: Phys 222, 223, 226 and 227.
Recommended for students in Genera! programmes.

courses.label: PHYS 325
courses.title: Atomic and Nuclear Physics 2
paras: Many electron atoms, atomic and X-ray spectra, nuclear structure, nuclear reactions, molecular and solid state physics.
Prereq: Phys 324. . Recommended for students in General programmes.

courses.label: PHYS 350
courses.title: Astrophysics 1
paras: Atomic and molecular spectra, forbidden and permitted transitions. Emission and absorption of radiation. Planck, Saha and Boltzmann equations. Line broadening effects. Radiation transfer theory. Sources of opacity. The spectra of the sun and stars.
Prereq: None, however familiarity with the contents of Phys 250-251 will be assumed. For third and fourth year students.

courses.label: PHYS 351
courses.title: Astrophysics 2
paras: Physical properties of the stars. Stellar distance determination. Distribution of the stars in space. The solar motion. Galactic rotation. Stellar dynamics. Characteristics and structure of our galaxy and external systems.
Prereq: None, however, familiarity with the contents - of Phys 250-251 will be assumed. For third and fourth year students.
Note
Phys 449, Phys 451, are also open to third and fourth year students. Phys 350 alternates with Phys 451 and Phys 351 alternates with Phys 449.

courses.label: PHYS 352
courses.title: Electronics 1
paras: A brief introduction to modern electronics including a discussion of semiconductors and solid state components. Basic electronic circuits including power supplies and amplifiers.
Prereq: Phys 122 or 243. Coreq: Phys 352L

courses.label: PHYS 352L
courses.title: Electronics 1 Laboratory
paras: For students taking Phys 352. Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 353
courses.title: Electronics 2
paras: A continuation of the study of electronic circuits. Introduction to simple digital circuits. Commonly used analogue and digital instruments.
Prereq: Phys 352. Coreq: 353L.

courses.label: PHYS 353L
courses.title: Electronice 2 Laboratory
paras: For students taking Phys 353. Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 354
courses.title: Atomic and Molecular Physics
paras: The Schrédinger equation applied to simple one-and three-dimension potentials, hydrogen atoms, angular momentum and spin, molecular vibrations and rotations, many electron atoms, radiation processes. Prereq: Phys 255.

courses.label: PHYS 355
courses.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
paras: Nuclear structure, interactions of nuclear radiations with matter, radioactive decay, nuclear reactions, nuclear force, elementary particles.
Prereq: Phys 255.
Course Descriptions Physics

courses.label: PHYS 358
courses.title: Thermodynamics
paras: Thermodynamic systems, equation of state, the laws of thermodynamics with applications. Change of phase.
Prereq: Math 213a-213b and a first year phys course.

courses.label: PHYS 359
courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
paras: Basic theory. Ideal classical and quantum gas. Occupation numbers. Effects of statistics. Applications to metals, perfect crystals, radiation and dense fluids.
Prereq: Phys 358

courses.label: PHYS 360A
courses.title: Intermediate Laboratory
paras: Selected experiments in mechanics, atomic physics, solid state physics, optics and electronics.
18 hours of experiments

courses.label: PHYS 360B
courses.title: Intermediate Laboratory
paras: Continuation of 360A.
18 hours of experiments

courses.label: PHYS 362
courses.title: Classical Mechanics 1
paras: Formal structure of classical mechanics with simple applications: foundations of Newtonian mechanics, dynamics of particles and systems of particles, linear oscillations, variational methods, Hamilton’s Principle, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian dynamics. Prereq: First year phys, Math 113, 213a-213b and 216. This course is primarily intended for Hons. Phys students.

courses.label: PHYS 363
courses.title: Classical Mechanics 2
paras: Application of the methods of classical mechanics to central force motion, nonlinear oscillations, twoparticle collisions, motion in noninertial frames, rigid body rotation, coupled oscillations.
Prereq: Phys 362. This course is primarily intended for Hons. Phys students.

courses.label: PHYS 364
courses.title: Mathematical Physics 1
paras: Vector analysis and applications. Vector operators using curvilinear coordinates. Cartesian tensors. Inertia tensor; stress, strain and rate of strain tensors. Applications to elasticity, fluids, electromagnetism and relativity.
Prereq: Math 213a-213b and 216. This course is primarily intended for Hons. Phys students.

courses.label: PHYS 365
courses.title: Mathematical Physics 2
paras: Fourier series, integral and transform with applications. Use of the Laplace transform in physics. Partial differential equations of mathematical physics. Separation of variables. Bessel and Legendre functions with application. Sturm-Liouville theory. Other special functions. Prereq: Math 213a-213b and 216. This course is primarily intended for Hons. Phys students.

courses.label: PHYS 368
courses.title: Geophysics 1
paras: Introductory topics on the physics of the earth. Seismology and the earth’s interior. Thermal history of the earth, gravity and isostasy. Origin of the continents and continental drift. (Identical to Earth 368).
Prereq: First year phys and calculus.

courses.label: PHYS 369
courses.title: Geophysics 2
paras: The geology of the ocean basins. Topics in physical oceanography. Physical properties of ocean water, heat budget of the world oceans. Oceanic circulations. Coriolis effects. Some idealized current regimes. (Identical to Earth 369).
Prereq: First year phys and calculus

courses.label: PHYS 371A
courses.title: Intermediate Laboratory
paras: Further experiments in atomic, nuclear and solid state physics, optics and electronics. For honours students who are taking Phys 360A.
18 hours experiments

courses.label: PHYS 371B
courses.title: Intermediate Laboratory
paras: Continuation of 371A.
For honours students who are taking Phys 360B. 18 hours experiments

courses.label: PHYS 380
courses.title: Molecular Biophysics
paras: Macromolecular structure and function, weak interactions, DNA replication, protein synthesis, energy production, photosynthesis, control of intracellular processes, structure of viruses; physical techniques.

courses.label: PHYS 381
courses.title: Cell Biophysics
paras: Structure and function of cellular membranes and organelles, membrane potentials and ion transport, nerve conduction, muscle contraction, vision and interaction of light with cells intercellular communication, growth control.
Course Descriptions 423 Physics

courses.label: PHYS 432
courses.title: Physics of Solid State Devices
paras: The theories of solid state physics are applied to explain the operation and use of several modern electronic devices, including the p-n junction, transistors, thyristors, tunnel diodes, field effect devices, optical devices, etc.
Prereq: Phys 435

courses.label: PHYS 433
courses.title: Experimental Research Project
paras: An experimental research project. This course is designed for students in the Honours Physics Programme and in the Co-operative Applied Physics programme.

Students in the regular Hons Phys programme must take either Phys 433 or Phys 437. Although students in the Co-operative Applied Phys (Hons) programme are recommended to take one of these courses, enrolment may be limited.

courses.label: PHYS 434A
courses.title: Introductory Quantum Mechanics
paras: Origins and necessity for quantum mechanics and its concepts and formulation. The Hamiltonian operator and Schrédinger’s equation, the harmonic oscillator (Schrédinger’s treatment). The uncertainty principle. Momentum representation. One dimensional potential problems. Angular momentum. The hydrogen atom.
Prereq: Phys 354

courses.label: PHYS 434B
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
paras: The matrix formulation of quantum mechanics. The harmonic oscillator (Heisenberg’s treatment). The matrices for angular momentum. Time-independent and time-dependent perturbation theory. The interaction of atomic systems with radiation. Multiparticle systems, identical particles. Pauli exclusion principle. The helium atom.
Prereq: Phys 434A
Note Phys 434B is strongly recommended for students intending to do graduate work.

courses.label: PHYS 435
courses.title: Solid State Physics
paras: Introductory concepts in crystal diffraction and the reciprocal lattice. Crystal bonding, lattice vibrations, thermal properties of insulators, free-electron theory of metals, band theory, semiconductors.
Prereq: Phys 255

courses.label: PHYS 437A
courses.title: Theoretical Physics Project
paras: Sellected subjects for advanced study by theoretically inclined students, topics in relativistic, quantum, and statistical physics.
Fall term enrolment will be limited.

Students in the regular Hons Phys programme must take either Phys 437A or Phys 433. Although students in the Co-operative Applied Phys (Hons) programme are recommended to take one of these courses, enrolment may be limited.

courses.label: PHYS 437B
courses.title: Continued Theoretical Physics Project
paras: A continuation and extension of the project initiated in Phys 437A. Available only to those students who have satisfactorily completed that portion of the project contained in Phys 437A in the immediately preceeding term..
Note
Students intending to take both Phys 437A and 437B must register for both courses, and have their registration approved by the Theoretical Physics Project co-ordinator, at the start of the Fall term.

courses.label: PHYS 441
courses.title: Electromagnetic Theory
paras: A generalized treatment of the basic laws of electricity and magnetism, mathematical techniques for the problems of electrostatics, solution of Maxwell’s equations in free space and the study of plane waves, theory of waveguides and introduction to radiation.
Prereq: Phys 222-223 or Phys 253, Phys 364-365.

courses.label: PHYS 442
courses.title: Structure of Solids
paras: A survey with emphasis on the physical properties and behaviour of metals and alloys. Elastic and plastic deformations of crystals. Solidification, structure of alloys, free energy of alloy systems, equilibrium diagrams, diffusion, solid state phase transformations.
Prereq: Phys 435

courses.label: PHYS 443
courses.title: Continuum Mechanics
paras: General description of continuum behaviour: stress, strain, rate of strain, constitutive relations, equations of motion, effect of symmetry, thermodynamics. Elastic media: Hooke’s law, simple problems, elastic waves. Fluids: classification, perfect fluids. Newtonian fluids, boundary layers, turbulence. Viscoelasticity, plastoelasticity. Applications to various systems.
Prereq: Phys 364-365
Course Descriptions Physics

courses.label: PHYS 444
courses.title: Nuclear Physics
paras: Elements of nuclear structures and systematics. Alpha emission, beta decay, gamma emission, twobody systems and nuclear forces, nuclear reactions. Neutron physics. Sub-nuclear particles.
Prereq: Phys 355

courses.label: PHYS 445
courses.title: Modern Optics
paras: The electromagnetic nature of light, polarization and coherence. Applications of temporal and spatial coherence. Quantum optics and photoelectric detection. Lasers, laser beam propagation, fiber optics. Elements of holography.
Prereq: Phys 256, 354 or equivalents.

courses.label: PHYS 449
courses.title: Radio Astronomy
paras: Radio telescopes. Radio sources including the sun. H I regions, H | regions. The galactic centre, pulsars, quasars, other extragalactic sources, cosmological implications.
Prereq: Phys 223 and Phys 250-251

courses.label: PHYS 450
courses.title: Astrophysics 3
paras: Solar system astrophysics (excluding the sun). The physical nature of planetary (and satellite) surfaces, atmospheres and interiors. Asteroids, meteorites and comets. The interplanetary medium (solar wind). Solar interactions with the interplanetary medium and earth’s magnetosphere.
Prereq: none, however, familiarity with the contents of Phys 250-257 will be assumed.

courses.label: PHYS 451
courses.title: Astrophysics 4
paras: The structure of stellar interiors, nuclear reactions and energy sources in the stars of the main sequence, early evolution of stars from the main sequence. Lifetimes of the stars.
Prereq: None, however, familiarity with the contents of Phys 250-251 will be assumed.
Note
Phys 350, Phys 351 are also open to third and fourth year students. Phys 350 and Phys 351 are offered in alternate years to Phys 449 and Phys 451.

courses.label: PHYS 452
courses.title: Electronics 3
paras: This course is meant to be of practical use to the experimentalist. Fundamental and advanced concepts of digital systems presented in terms of modern techniques. A brief treatment of microprocessors and minicomputers.
Prereq: Phys 352-353.

courses.label: PHYS 453
courses.title: Electronics 4
paras: A variety of topics in the operation of systems. Transistors, modern circuit techniques, noise, stability under feedback, information theory, and possible student motivated topics. Includes laboratory demonstrations.
Prereq: Phys 352-353

courses.label: PHYS 464
courses.title: Mathematical Physics 3
paras: Applications to Physics of the theory of functions of a complex variable.
Prereq: Phys 364-365

courses.label: PHYS 465
courses.title: Mathematical Physics 4
paras: Theory and applications of integral transforms, integral equations and ‘Green's functions. Numerical Methods.
Prereq: Phys 464

courses.label: PHYS 480
courses.title: Radiation Biophysics
paras: The effect of radiation of various kinds on cells and tissues, exposure calculations, mechanism of damage, repair theories, genetic effect, target theory, isotopic tracers in biophysical research.
». Phys 481 WwW 3C 0.5
Biophysics of Organ Systems
Physics of hemeostasis, interactions with the
environment, circulation of blood, temperature regulation, respiration, transport problems and special organ systems.

courses.label: PHYS 482
courses.title: Biophysics of Nervous Systems
paras: Neurons; nerve conduction, sensory transducers; coding, processing and storage of information; control of muscles and other effector organs. Recommended for third or fourth year students in Math, Eng, Sci or HKLS.
Course Descriptions 425

courses.label: PSCI 281
courses.title: International Politics 1
paras: P Sci 282 international Politics 2

courses.label: PSCI 481
courses.title: Research Seminar on World Politics Psychology
paras: Psych 254 Psych 316 Psych 333 Psych 353

courses.label: PSCI 101
courses.title: Introduction to Politics 1
paras: An introduction to the nature of politics and to the conflict of modern political ideas. The course involves a common lecture series and tutorials led by faculty members.
Note
Political Science 102 consists of a series of courses dealing with different aspects of politics. Students Should select the course which most closely corresponds to their interests.

courses.label: PSCI 102A
courses.title: Imperialism in International Relations
paras: A discussion of the idea of imperialism in ancient and modern international relation, the causes and motives of imperialism, changes in imperial strategies, and the difference between the ‘old’ and the ‘new’ imperialism.

courses.label: PSCI 102C
courses.title: Politics in Action
paras: An examination of the way in which society’s conflicting demands are organized, articulated, and translated in action. The part played by the various political and economic forces in society will be examined in a comparative framework.

courses.label: PSCI 102D
courses.title: The Political Process in the Modern Democracies
paras: A study of power and influence in the modern democracies, based on an examination of three contending models in the political process - the liberal-democractic or popular rule model, the pluralist model, and the elitist model.

courses.label: PSCI 102E
courses.title: Political Rights and Obligations
paras: An introductory examination of the idea of individual rights as a timitation on legitimate governmental authority, the possible grounds for such claimed rights, and their relationship to political obligations (duties).

courses.label: PSCI 102H
courses.title: Citizen Participation in Canada
paras: Not offered 1980-81

courses.label: PSCI 102K
courses.title: Mass Political Violence
paras: A distinctive social feature of our century is the amount of political violence. Man-made deaths number approximately one hundred-million. This course will describe and evaluate various theories of political violence.

courses.label: PSCI 102M
courses.title: Contemporary Issues in Canadian Public Policy
paras: An evaluation of various public policy responses to some contemporary Canadian social, cultural, economic, environmental, and political problems, as well as the process of policy-making.

courses.label: PSCI 214
courses.title: Quantitative Analysis
paras: An introduction to the use of quantitative methods in Political Science. Only a rudimentary understanding of mathematics is required.
Prereq: Second year standing
Course Descriptions Political Science

courses.label: PSCI 225
courses.title: The History of Political Theory 1
paras: A survey of the principal ideas of Western political theorists from the earliest times to the seventeenth century.
Prereq: Second year standing

courses.label: PSCI 226
courses.title: The History of Political Theory 2
paras: A survey of the principal ideas of Western political theorists since the seventeenth century.
Prereq: Second year standing

courses.label: PSCI 253
courses.title: Comparative Communism 1
paras: An examination of the historical development of the communist international system, the cause of its diversity and doctrinal variety, with emphasis on common problems and the role of ruling parties, their objectives, performance, and strategy.
Prereq: Second year standing

courses.label: PSCI 254
courses.title: Comparative Communism 2
paras: This course will concentrate on contemporary issues in communist politics, examining selected ruling and non-ruling communist parties.
Prereq: Political Science 253 or Consent of the instructor

courses.label: PSCI 260
courses.title: Canadian Government and Politics
paras: An analysis of the structure and practices of the Canadian political system.
Prereq: Second year standing

courses.label: PSCI 260A
courses.title: Canadian Government and Politics 1
paras: The first half of P Sci 260, for students in cooperative programmes only.
No prereq for students in the second year and above

courses.label: PSCI 260B
courses.title: Canadian Government and Politics 2
paras: The second half of P Sci 260, for students in cooperative programmes only.
Prereq: P Sci 260A or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 264
courses.title: American Government and Politics
paras: The theory and practice of the American political system as revealed by the institutions and operations of American national government.
No prereq for students in the second year and above

courses.label: PSCI 268
courses.title: British Government and Politics
paras: An examination of the uniquely British characteristics of the British political system.
No prereq for students in the second year or above

courses.label: PSCI 271
courses.title: Political Behaviour 1
paras: An examination of the impact of behaviouralism upon the study of politics, focusing on the methodological assumptions and aspirations of behaviouralism.
No prereq for students in the second year and above

courses.label: PSCI 272
courses.title: Political Behaviour 2
paras: An examination of the political attitudes and behaviour of men and women in different political systems.
Prereq: P Sci 271 or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 281
courses.title: International Politics 1
paras: This course studies the transformation of the international system stressing East-West, Rich-Poor, and North-South perspectives and interactions.
No prereq for students in the second year and above

courses.label: PSCI 282
courses.title: International Politics 2
paras: This course studies the roots of foreign policy behaviour of selected western and non-western (particularly Asian) states.
Prereq: P Sci 281 or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 291
courses.title: The Canadian Legal Process
paras: An analysis of the manner in which the Common Law functions, together with an examination of the structure and jurisdiction of the Canadian court systems. Taught by a member of the legal profession.
Prereq: Open to all students in the second year and above

courses.label: PSCI 292
courses.title: Aspects of Canadian Law
paras: A study of the way in which the law reflects and influences political ideas and attitudes in Canada in relation to a number of aspects of Canadian life. Taught by a member of the legal profession.
Prereq: Open to all students in the second year and above
Course Descriptions 427 Political Science

courses.label: PSCI 293
courses.title: Political Journalism
paras: An account of the special factors affecting political reporting and commentary in the broadcast and frint media, with a critical evaluation of contemporary practice in the field. Taught by a practising journalist.
No prereq for students in the second year and above

courses.label: PSCI 311
courses.title: Methodology of Political Science: The Foundations
paras: A selective examination of seminal works which have contributed to our understanding of the methods appropriate to the study of politics. Not a survey course.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor

courses.label: PSCI 312
courses.title: Approaches to Survey Analysis in Political Science
paras: This course introduces students with previous experience in statistical methods to the special problems associated with the analysis of the nominal data collected in surveys.
Prereq: P Sci 214

courses.label: PSCI 315
courses.title: Research Design in Political Science
paras: Introduction to the logic and limitations of experimental and non-experimental research designs. Selected studies of politics are examined to demonstrate how plausible threats to validity are made less plausible with appropriate design and data analysis.
Prereq: P Sci 214 or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 321
courses.title: Marxist Theory
paras: An examination of the formation of Marx’s method and of its significance for the proletariat.
No prereq for students in the third year and above

courses.label: PSCI 322
courses.title: Marxism and Revolution After Marx
paras: A selective study of developments in Marxist theory and political movements after Marx.
Prereq: P Sci 321

courses.label: PSCI 323
courses.title: Ancient Political Philosophy
paras: A selective examination of political philosophy during the classical period in Greece.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor

courses.label: PSCI 324
courses.title: Modern Political Philosophy
paras: A selective examination of political philosophy in the modern period.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 325
courses.title: Radical Political Theory
paras: A discussion of non-marxian political ideas such as social gospel, populism, fascism and Fabian socialism, and their socio-economic roots and sources.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor

courses.label: PSCI 327
courses.title: Political Science and Political Values
paras: An examination of the relationship of ‘‘values” to a proper science of politics.
Prereq: Consent of instructor
Alternates with P Sci 311

courses.label: PSCI 331
courses.title: Public Administration 1
paras: An introduction to the principles of public administration illustrated by the study of Canadian institutions largely at the federal level, but including provincial and municipal examples.
Prereq: P Sci 260 or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 332
courses.title: Public Administration 2
paras: Analyses of problems and issues in the field applying the knowledge gained in P Sci 331. Prereq: P Sci 331 or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 343
courses.title: Provincial Politics
paras: A comparative analysis of the political systems of the Canadian provinces which explores the possibility that as many as ten political cultures exist in Canada.
Prereq: P Sci 260

courses.label: PSCI 342
courses.title: Politics in Quebec
paras: A seminar dealing with the political and social development of Quebec. The emphasis will be on the problems and issues of contemporary Quebec. Prereq: P Sci 260 or 341 or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 343
courses.title: Canadian Municipal Government
paras: A study of the assumptions, structures, and performance of municipal government in Canada with reference to metropolitan and regional structural innovations (particularly in Ontario).
Open to students in the third year and above with at least one previous course in Political Science
Course Descriptions Political Science

courses.label: PSCI 344
courses.title: The Politics of Local Government
paras: A study of the political process in selected Canadian cities focusing on citizen participation, internal decision-making, leadership, and the allocation of power.
Prereq: P Sci 343 or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 350
courses.title: The Politics of the Developing Areas
paras: An examination of selected topics in the politics of developing areas, with emphasis on the theoretical and empirical adequacy of explanations of macro and micro political and economic change in Asia, Africa and Latin America.
No prereq for students in the third year or above

courses.label: PSCI 350A
courses.title: The Politics of the Developing Areas 1
paras: The first half of P Sci 350.
No prereq for students in the third year or above

courses.label: PSCI 350B
courses.title: The Politics of the Developing Areas 2
paras: The second half of P Sci 350. May be taken separately.
No prereq for students in the third year or above

courses.label: PSCI 351
courses.title: Comparative Federal Systems
paras: A comparative examination of federal systems, with an emphasis on the problems and processes of integration and disintegration.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor

courses.label: PSCI 352
courses.title: Comparative Legislative Systems
paras: A comparison of the institutional and behavioural characteristics of legislatures in a comparative framework, with emphasis on Canada, the United States, Great Britain, and Australia.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor

courses.label: PSCI 362
courses.title: Soviet Government and Politics
paras: An intensive survey of the development of Soviet political structures with analysis of the relative influence of ideological goals on the one hand and social forces on the other.
Prereq: P Sci 253-254 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 364
courses.title: Politics in Italy
paras: An examination of the social, economic, and ideological forces underlying contemporary politics in Italy.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 371
courses.title: Political Culture
paras: An analysis of the development of the concept of political culture as an analytical tool.
Prereq: P Sci 271/272 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 273
courses.title: Political Parties
paras: An examination of the relationship of political parties and party systems to the dynamics of social change taking into account the imperatives of survival and adaption and the dilemma of principles versus power.
Prereq: At least one of P Sci 260, 262, 264, 268, 271, or 272.

courses.label: PSCI 374
courses.title: Interest Group Politics
paras: A study.of interest group theory and comparative analysis of the internal politics of interest groups and their role in the political process.
Prereq: At least one of P Sci 260, 262, 264, 268, 271, or 272.

courses.label: PSCI 380
courses.title: World Politics
paras: An examination of the structure or institutional arrangements of global society and their interrelationships with interstate war and the allocation of misery. A wide range of theories of international violence and imperialism will be considered.
Open only to students in the third year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 380A
courses.title: World Politics 1
paras: The first half of P Sci 380.
Open only to students in the third year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 380B
courses.title: World Politics 2
paras: The second half of P Sci 380.
Open only to students in the third year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 390
courses.title: Special Studies
paras: From time to time courses of special study may be added to the programme at the third year level. Students wishing to add such courses should consult the Department’s Undergraduate Officer.

courses.label: PSCI 411
courses.title: Theories and Methods of Political Science
paras: An examination and evaluation of explanations of political phenomena with the emphasis upon the criteria with which to compare competing theories and the methods of analysis which are appropriate to a given problem.
Prereq: Fourth year honours standing and consent of instructor.
Course Descriptions 429 Political Science

courses.label: PSCI 424
courses.title: Contemporary Socialist and Communist Thought
paras: This course examines recent trends in Marxist theory and its contribution to the analysis of capitalist and socialist societies.
Prereq: Consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 425
courses.title: English Political Theory of the Nineteenth Century
paras: Not offered 1980-81.

courses.label: PSCI 426
courses.title: Selected Subjects in Political Philosophy
paras: A selective treatment of basic themes in political philosophy in the modern and pre-modern periods. For third year Political Science students, but open to others with prereq P Sci 221, 222, 323, or 324, or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 427
courses.title: Special Topics in Politcal Philosophy
paras: A selective examination of basic problems in political philosophy in the modern and pre-modern periods.
Prereq: P Sci 221, 222, 323 or 324.

courses.label: PSCI 428
courses.title: State and Economic Life
paras: An analytical and comparative study of the growth of government intervention in the economic process, and of the development of the welfare state.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 435
courses.title: The Politics of Canadian Resource Development
paras: A seminar focussing on the strategies of resource development policies, with an emphasis on the economic, political, environmental and cultural implications of oil, natural gas, and mineral exploitation.
Prereq: Consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 436
courses.title: Comparative Public Policy
paras: A comparative examination of public policy and approaches to the study of public policy, with case studies from Germany, Britain, France, Sweden, Canada, the United States and India.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 442
courses.title: Politics in Ontario
paras: A critical examination of the distinctive eiements of government and politics in the Province of Ontario. Prereq: P Sci 260 or 341 or consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 443
courses.title: Politics In Western Canada
paras: A critical examination of the distinctive elements of government and politics in the provinces of Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Alberta, and British Columbia.
Prereq: P Sci 260 or 341 or consent of instructor. Alternates with P Sci 445.

courses.label: PSCI 445
courses.title: Politics in the Atlantic Provinces
paras: A critical examination of the distinctive elements of government and politics in the provinces of Newfoundland, Prince Edward Island, Nova Scotia, and New Brunswick.
Prereq: P Sci 341. Alternates with P Sci 443.

courses.label: PSCI 451
courses.title: Comparative Parliamentary Systems
paras: An analytical comparison of parliamentary institutions and processes as they have developed in various political systems influenced by Britain. Prereq: P Sci 251 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 453
courses.title: Problems in Comparative Politics 1
paras: A critical examination of contending approaches to the study of comparative politics.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 454
courses.title: Problems in Comparative Politics 2
paras: A critical examination of selected topics in the politics of Western Europe.
Prereq: P Sci 453.

courses.label: PSCI 461
courses.title: Problems in Canadian Politics 1
paras: A critical examination of various problems of Canadian politics, with an emphasis on political integration, federalism and political parties. Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 462
courses.title: Problems in Canadian Politics 2
paras: A senior research course on selected aspects of Canadian political life, with emphasis on the preparation of a major and original research paper. For fourth year Political Science students but open to others with prereq P Sci 461.

courses.label: PSCI 471
courses.title: Public Opinion and Propaganda
paras: Not offered 1980-81.
Course Descriptions Political Science

courses.label: PSCI 473
courses.title: Voting Behaviour
paras: A comparative study of the motivations underlying electoral choice in Canada, Great Britain and the United States.
Prereq: P Sci 214, 373 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 475
courses.title: Political Socialization
paras: A study of the processes and agents of political socialization and their effects on political stability or change in liberal-democratic societies.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 476
courses.title: Research Seminar in Political Behaviour
paras: A research-oriented seminar on selected theoretical works in political behaviour, with an emphasis on the development of research projects dealing with Canadian topics.
Prereq: Consent on the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 479
courses.title: Senior Research Seminar: Violence in the Political Process
paras: Politics can be brutal. This seminar deals with violence in the political process. The focus is on the relationships between the society and the coercive apparatus of the state.
Prereq: Third or Fourth Year standing.

courses.label: PSCI 481
courses.title: Research Seminar on World Politics
paras: An examination of research on the causes and consequences of interstate warfare.
Prereq: P Sci 380 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 483
courses.title: Comparative Foreign Relations 1
paras: This focuses on the theoretical literature dealing with (1) the nature of the international system, and (2) various approaches to the study of foreign policy with a particular emphasis on decision-making and bargaining.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor only.

courses.label: PSCI 484
courses.title: Comparative Foreign Relations 2

Prereq: P Sci 281-282 or third or fourth year standing.

courses.label: PSYCH 101
courses.title: Introductory Psychology
paras: A general survey course designed to provide the student with an understanding of the basic concepts and techniques of modern psychology as a behavioural science.
Also offered at Renison and St. Jerome's Colleges

courses.label: PSYCH 102
courses.title: Introductory Psychology Special Topics
paras: A study in greater depth of selected broad issues and problems introduced in Psychology 101.
Also offered at Renison and St. Jerome’s Colleges

courses.label: PSYCH 102A
courses.title: Applied Psychology
paras: Applications of Psychological research to contemporary problems: man and environment, human factors engineering, management and organizations, crime and violence, and public health.

courses.label: PSYCH 102B
courses.title: Nature, Nurture and Human Behaviour
paras: The role of heredity and environment in the development of intelligence, personality and personality disorders, and conflict and aggression.

courses.label: PSYCH 102C
courses.title: Culture’s Influence on Behaviour
paras: The role of culture on the development of Perception, Cognition, Learning, and memory; cultural influences on personality and personality disorders, and on conflict and aggression.

courses.label: PSYCH 102D
courses.title: Psychology of Consciousness
paras: Modes of thinking, emotion, creativity, and altered states of consciousness.

courses.label: PSYCH 200
courses.title: Measurement in Psychology
paras: The logic of measurement in Psychology. Descriptive procedures for collecting and handling data. Making interences from test scores. The use of correlational procedures in measuring intelligence, achievement, aptitudes, interests and personality.

courses.label: PSYCH 201
courses.title: Statistical Methods in Psychology
paras: An introduction to data analysis. Topics covered include descriptive statistics and the logic and methods of inferential statistics with emphasis on applications in psychology. Little mathematics background is assumed.

courses.label: PSYCH 202
courses.title: Experimental Design
paras: An examination of the effective use and interpretation of statistics in design and understanding of experiments in the social sciences. Prereq: Psych 201

courses.label: PSYCH 203
courses.title: Learning and Motivation
paras: This course is designed to introduce the student to theories in Learning and Motivation and to provide the student with an understanding of the experimental techniques in these areas.
Prereq: Psych 101

courses.label: PSYCH 206
courses.title: Perceptual Processes
paras: An examination of data and theory concerning perceptual processes. Topics will include the perception of form and space, perceptual learning and a consideration of the effect of personality variables in perception.
Prereq: Psych 107

courses.label: PSYCH 207
courses.title: Cognitive Processes
paras: An examination and evaluation of selected topics dealing with human learning, thinking, concept formation, memory and language.
Prereq: Psych 101

courses.label: PSYCH 211
courses.title: Development Psychology
paras: An examination of the process and factors of human development.
Prereq: Psych 107
Also offered at St. Jerome's College

courses.label: PSYCH 212
courses.title: Educational Psychology
paras: A consideration of the main variables affecting learning in the classroom with special focus upon the conditions essential to efficient learning. Prereq: Psych 101
Also offered at St. Jerome’s College

courses.label: PSYCH 213
courses.title: Exceptional Children
paras: Educational problems associated with mental retardation, emotional disturbances, sensory and physical impairments and intellectual giftedness.

courses.label: PSYCH 214
courses.title: Psychology of Adolescence
paras: A study of the psychological processes in the second decade of human development. Consideration is given to such areas as intellectual, emotional and social growth, and identity formation. Current concepts, issues, and research are stressed. Prereq: Psych 211
Also offered at St. Jerome’s College
Course Descriptions 433 Psychology

courses.label: PSYCH 218
courses.title: Aging, Dying and Death
paras: An examination of the psychological aspects of aging and the traditional and recent literature relating to various views on the reality of death in the life of man. Therapy with dying individuals are reviewed and evaluated.
Prereq: Psych 101
Offered at St. Jerome’s College

courses.label: PSYCH 231
courses.title: Psychology of Religious Experience
paras: Approaches of traditional psychological theories and especially of a modern psychology of consciousness toward phenomena of religious experience, mysticism and meditation are examined. The transcendant phenomena are compared with other altered states of consciousness.
Prereq: Psych 101
Offered at St. Jerome’s College

courses.label: PSYCH 236
courses.title: A Psychological Analysis of Human Sexuality
paras: This course will examine. psychological and social psychological theories and empirical investigations of human sexuality.
Prereq: Psych 101 or permission of instructor Offered at St. Jerome’s College

courses.label: PSYCH 253
courses.title: Social Psychology
paras: An introduction to theories and research on people in their physical and social environment. Typically, topics such as conformity, persuasion, attraction, prejudice, communication, aggression, the psychology of freedom, justice and human exchange will be introduced.
Prereq: Psych 101
Cross-listed as Psych 220R

courses.label: PSYCH 254
courses.title: Interpersonal Relations
paras: A psychological analysis of social interaction. The development of interpersonal attraction from first impressions to long-term relationships. The roots of hostility, conflict and communication problems. Prereq: Psych 253
Cross-listed as Psych 227R

courses.label: PSYCH 258
courses.title: Principles and Evoiution of Psychoanalytic Thought
paras: This course expresses the fundamental psychoanalytic vision as articulated by Sigmund Freud, and its relevance to the humanities. The . theme is to understand the potentially liberating spirit which is at the root of psychoanalysis. Prereq: Psych 101
Offered at St. Jerome’s College

courses.label: PSYCH 261
courses.title: Physiological Psychology
paras: The structure and function of the nervous system and their relation to behaviour.
Prereq: Psych 101 or permission of instructor

courses.label: PSYCH 271
courses.title: Animal Behaviour
paras: An indepth study of the behaviour of animals emphasizing both observational and experimental research.
Prereq: Psych 101 or permission of instructor

courses.label: PSYCH 293
courses.title: Research in Learning and Motivation
paras: Open only to students in a Psychology Programme (Honours, Joint Honours, General or Minor Programmes).
Prereq: Psych 201 and one of Psych 203 or 271

courses.label: PSYCH 295
courses.title: Research in Perceptual and Cognitive Processes Open only to students in a Psychology Programme (Honours, Joint Honours, General or Minor
paras: Programmes).
Prereq: Psych 201 and one of Psych 206 or 207

courses.label: PSYCH 297
courses.title: Research in Biopsychology
paras: Open only to students in a Psychology Programme (Honours, Joint Honours, General or Minor Programmes).
Prereq: Psych 201 and Psych 261

courses.label: PSYCH 301
courses.title: Tests and Measurement
paras: An introduction to the theory and use of psychological tests. Special emphasis is placed on the assessment of personality, inteiligence, aptitudes and interests.
Prereq: Psych 201

courses.label: PSYCH 305
courses.title: Sensory Processes
paras: Not offered 1980-81

courses.label: PSYCH 307
courses.title: Cognitive Neurology
paras: Not offered 1980-81 Cross listed as Kin 456 which is offered in 1980-81

courses.label: PSYCH 311
courses.title: Behaviour and Development of Human Infants
paras: The purposes of this course are to study the behaviour and development of human infants, to gain direct experience with infants, and to examine community attitudes and resources available for infant care.
Prereq: Psych 211 or permission of instructor
Course Descriptions Psychology

courses.label: PSYCH 312
courses.title: Learning Disabilities
paras: A critical examination of the concept of learning disability and of current issues in the assessment and remediation of learning problems.
Prereq: Psych 211 or Psych 212 or Psych 213 Also offered at St. Jerome's College

courses.label: PSYCH 316
courses.title: Moral Development
paras: Not offered 1980-81

courses.label: PSYCH 317
courses.title: The Emotionally Disturbed Child
paras: A review of traditional concepts, current thoughts and major research on the psychopathology of childhood. Specific attention will be given to socialization processes and educational procedures. Prereq: Psych 211
Offered at St. Jerome’s College

courses.label: PSYCH 322
courses.title: Principles and Practice in Early Childhood Education |
paras: Current principles of teaching preschool-aged children. An emphasis is placed on those curricula which aim to foster social and cognitive development. Topics include: characteristics and needs of children in group-care settings; classroom management; curriculum planning.
Prereq: Acceptance into the Early Childhood Education and Care Option

courses.label: PSYCH 323
courses.title: Practicum in Early Childhood Education |
paras: Directed supervision with young children in group settings. The course requires 3 hours of field work per week. Must be taken concurrently with Psych 322.
Prereq: Acceptance into the Early Childhood Education and Care Option

courses.label: PSYCH 331
courses.title: Individual Differences
paras: An analysis of individual and group differences in behaviour, with emphasis on studies of intetligence. Prereq: Psych 200 or Psych 301

courses.label: PSYCH 333
courses.title: Industrial Psychology
paras: An introduction to the methods and problems in Industrial Psychology.
Prereq: Psych 101

courses.label: PSYCH 334
courses.title: Theories of Counselling Psychology
paras: An introduction to the methods, theories and problems in Counseiling Psychology.
Prereq: Psych 101
Also offered at Renison and St. Jerome's Colleges

courses.label: PSYCH 335
courses.title: Personality and Behaviour Change
paras: Forms of psychological intervention that produce important changes in the way people think, feel and behave including psychoanalysis, behaviour therapy, brainwashing, cult conversions, deprogramming, hypnosis, biofeedback and meditation.
Prereq: Psych 101

courses.label: PSYCH 339
courses.title: Personnel Psychology
paras: An examination of the following major topics in personnel psychology: employment planning, selection and recruitment, selection techniques, career development, performance appraisal, training programmes, labour relations, compensations systems.
Prereq: Psych 333

courses.label: PSYCH 340
courses.title: Community Psychology
paras: Not offered 1980-81

courses.label: PSYCH 341
courses.title: Psychology of Early Childhood Education
paras: An introduction to theories and issues in early childhood education. Topics include issues differentiating preschool programmes and application of psychological theory/research to early education.
Prereq: Psych 211

courses.label: PSYCH 350
courses.title: Group and Individual Counselling
paras: The practice of counselling in terms of current psychological theories and research. The demonstration and development of these concepts are aided by personal participation, exercises, role play and videotape stimulation.
Prereq: Psych 355, 357, and 334 or suitable alternative and permission of instructor
Offered at St. Jerome’s College

courses.label: PSYCH 353
courses.title: Aggression and Social Conflict
paras: This course will examine the genetic, physiological, and social causes of aggression, with the emphasis on social-psychological causes.
Prereq: Psych 253
Course Descriptions 435 Psychology

courses.label: PSYCH 354
courses.title: Interpersonal Processes in Critical Situations
paras: The course will examine reactions to victims of misfortunes such as serious physical and mental illness, natural disaster, poverty and discrimination. Prereq: Psych 253

courses.label: PSYCH 355
courses.title: Personality Theory
paras: An examination and evaluation of some of the outstanding theories of personality.
Prereq: Psych 107
Cross-listed as Psych 322R

courses.label: PSYCH 357
courses.title: Psychopathology
paras: The nature and origin of deviant behaviour. Prereq: Psych 101
Cross-listed as Psych 323R
Also offered at St. Jerome’s Callege

courses.label: PSYCH 359
courses.title: Personality and Adjustment
paras: A study of theory and research related to the adaptation and to the function of personality in a variety of natural and artificial settings. The focus is on normal behaviour.
Prereq: Psych 355

courses.label: PSYCH 363
courses.title: Special Subjects
paras: One or more half courses will be offered at different times as announced by the Department.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: PSYCH 370
courses.title: Cross-Cultural Psychology
paras: An examination of the influence of cultural differences on perceptual-cagnitive processes, personality characteristics, and psychopathology. Prereq: A minimum of two half courses in Psychology

courses.label: PSYCH 372
courses.title: Environmental Psychology
paras: This course is intended to increase the awareness and understanding of the impact of the environment on human behaviour and experience. Topics to be discussed include: spacing, territoriality, crowding, subjective impressions of environments, and research paradigms.
Prereq: Psych 101 and 201 or permission of instructor.
Offered at St. Jerome's College

courses.label: PSYCH 393
courses.title: Research in Development Psychology
paras: Open only to students in a Psychology Programme (Honours, Joint Honours, General or Minor Programmes).
Prereq: Psych 201 and 211

courses.label: PSYCH 395
courses.title: Research in Social Psychology
paras: Open only to students in a Psychology Programme (Honours, Joint Honours, General or Minor Programmes).
Prereq: Psych 201 and 253

courses.label: PSYCH 397
courses.title: Research in Personality and Psychopathology Open only to students in a Psychology Programme (Honours, Joint Honours, General or Minor
paras: Programmes).
Prereq: Psych 201 and one of Psych 355 or 357

courses.label: PSYCH 410
courses.title: History and Systems
paras: An examination of current theoretical approaches to psychological problems present in an historical context.

courses.label: PSYCH 422
courses.title: Principles and Practice in Early Childhood Education Il
paras: An examination of the various aspects of planning and administration in early childhood education programmes. Topics include: practical applications of Piaget’s theory; parent education.
Prereq: Psych 322 and 323

courses.label: PSYCH 423
courses.title: Practicum in Early Childhood Education Il
paras: Practicum for advanced students in early childhood education. The course requires 6 hours of field work per week in preschool, kindergarten or daycare settings. Must be taken concurrently with Psychology 422.
Prereq: Psych 322 and 323

Also offered at St. Jerome’s College

courses.label: PSYCH 498
courses.title: Senior Honours Essay - Review Paper
paras: Each student will work under the direction of a member of the department on a critical integrative review of an issue in research literature. The result of this review will be presented in the form of a thesis, which will be critically examined by members of the department.
Also offered at St. Jerome’s College

The following courses are administered by Renison College. Since these courses are intended primarily for students in the Social Development programme, students planning a General or Honours Psychology programme must consult their faculty advisor concerning Psychology major credit for these courses.

courses.label: PSYCH 398R
courses.title: Independent Study (Open to senior Social Development Studies majors only)
paras: Course Descriptions 437

courses.label: PSYCH 120R
courses.title: Introductory Psychology
paras: Basic concepts and techniques of modern psychology as a behavioural science. The development of behaviour, learning and remembering, motivation, values and attitudes, personality, sensation and perception, and small group processes will be studied with reference to physiological correlates.

courses.label: PSYCH 121R
courses.title: Introductory Psychology (Special Topics)
paras: A more in-depth study of selected topics introduced in Psych 120R.
Prereq: Psych 120R

courses.label: PSYCH 220R
courses.title: Social Psychology
paras: An examination of psychological principles invoived in the interaction of the individual and society. Topics include conformity, attitude formation, prejudice, attraction, aggression, pro-sacial behaviour, social psychology of sexual attitudes. (Cross-listed with Psych 253)
Prereq: An introductory psychology course

courses.label: PSYCH 221R
courses.title: Interpersonal Interaction
paras: A consideration of theories and research into interpersonal interaction. Topics include H. S. Sullivan; Double Bind Theory; Non-verbal Behaviour; Transactional Analysis; R. D. Laing; Interaction Approaches to Personality; Social Exchange; balance, attribution and reinforcement theories, complementary needs; rules of encounter. (Cross-listed with Psych 254)
Prereq: Psych 220R or Psych 253

courses.label: PSYCH 322R
courses.title: Personality (Personality Theory)
paras: An examination of the major theories of personality including consideration of the psychoanalytic, dispositional, humanistic, and behaviouristic models, (Cross-listed with Psych 355)
Prereq: An introductory psychology course

courses.label: PSYCH 323R
courses.title: Abnormal Psychology (Psychopathology)
paras: A consideration of the theory and research in the area of abnormal psychology.
(Cross-listed with Psych 357)
Prereq: An introductory psychology course

courses.label: PSYCH 334R
courses.title: Theories of Counselling Psychology
paras: An introduction to the theories, methods and problems in Counselling Psychology. Prereq: An introductory psychology course

courses.label: PSYCH 367R
courses.title: Special Topics in Psychology
paras: One or more half courses will be offered from time to time as announed by the Social Development Studies Programme. Subjects will be dependent upon special research and/or instructional interests of faculty.

courses.label: PSYCH 369R
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Counselling Psychology
paras: An in-depth study of special topics arising in Psych 334 (R)
Prereq: Psych 334 (R)

Psych 398R/399R independent Studies An independent in-depth study of a selected area of concern to the student within the discipline of psychology. courses.label: REC 100
courses.title: Introduction to the Study of Leisure and Recreation
paras: An overview of the total field of recreation emphasizing the understanding of leisure phenomena and implications for contemporary society.

courses.label: REC 101
courses.title: Introduction to Leisure Services
paras: An introduction to various leisure service agencies and the services provided. Field trips to municipalities, specialized institutions, and voluntary agencies.

courses.label: REC 200
courses.title: Theories of Play
paras: A critical analysis of definitions, concepts and assumptions of classical, recent and modern theories of play with implications for research strategies, programming and planning for play.

courses.label: REC 201
courses.title: Leisure and the Social Sciences
paras: Examination of modern methodological and theoretical approaches to the study of leisure behaviour with emphasis upon the socio-cultural, socio-psychological and economic dimensions.

courses.label: REC 204
courses.title: Leisure and Recreation in Historical Perspective
paras: Analysis of socio-cultural determinants which have influenced Canadian Leisure behaviour.
Prereq: Rec 100 or consent of instructor

courses.label: REC 210
courses.title: Organization and Administration of Recreation Services
paras: The organization and administration of recreation on federal, provincial and municipal levels; legislation, financing, budgeting, problem solving, public relations, administrative practices and departmental organization with particular emphasis on the municipal level.

courses.label: REC 220
courses.title: Recreation Programme Development
paras: A study of the scope of community recreation programmes and the factors involved in programme leadership. Emphasis will be placed on the goals in recreation for the leader and participant, effective leadership of individuals and groups, individual and group creativity.
Course Descriptions Recreation

courses.label: REC 230
courses.title: Introduction to Outdoor Recreation
paras: A study of outdoor recreation in relation to contemporary lifestyles, natural and human resource systems. Includes the examination of outdoor settings as an integral part of an outdoor recreation continuum. Includes the role of selected governmental and non-governmental bodies.

courses.label: REC 241
courses.title: Administration of Camping and Outdoor Education
paras: The philosophy and objectives of camping and outdoor education; administration, organizing, planning, staff relationships, leadership training, trends in camping and outdoor education. The emphasis in this course will be the place of the resident camp in education and recreation.
Prereq: Rec 230

courses.label: REC 250
courses.title: Introduction to Recreation for Special Populations
paras: Examines the philosophical, theoretical and empirical frameworks of recreation as a therapeutic service and process to individuals with physical, emotional and intellectual disabilities.

courses.label: REC 252
courses.title: Recreation and Mental Retardation
paras: An analysis of the motoric and psycho-social behavioral dimensions specific to the retarded with direct and obvious applicability to the planning, implementing and evaluating of recreational programmes.
Prereq: Rec 250, Psych 242

courses.label: REC 253
courses.title: Recreation and Physical Disabilities
paras: The psycho-social aspects of physical disabilities will be analysed, with special focus given to the planning, implementing and evaluating of leisure activities.
Prereq: Rec 250, permission of instructor

courses.label: REC 254
courses.title: Recreation and Mental Health
paras: A psycho-social analysis of the determinants and consequences of recreative behaviour as related to positive and negative mental health, discussing in detail, structure, semiotic factors and interaction patterns.
Prereq: Rec 250

courses.label: REC 270
courses.title: Statistical Techniques Applied to Leisure Studies
paras: An introduction to descriptive and inferential Statistics and the interpretation of data. A major consideration of the course is the use of statistics in the solution of problems in recreation and leisure.

courses.label: REC 300
courses.title: Philosophy of Leisure
paras: Examination of major philosophical themes through the ages with reference to contemporary viability and effect upon social behaviour.
Prereq: Consent of instructor, third year standing

courses.label: REC 301
courses.title: Sociology of Leisure (Soc 375)
paras: Nature and extent of leisure phenomena in contemporary society. Examination of institutional and formal organizational aspects, social role, social research strategies employed in the study of leisure. Prereq: Two term courses in Sociology

courses.label: REC 302
courses.title: Travel and Tourism
paras: The scope and nature of travel and tourism as contemporary leisure experiences. Economic, political and social ramifications, research strategies employed, implications for the future.
Prereq: Rec 301

courses.label: REC 303
courses.title: Sport in Societry (Kin 452)
paras: An introduction to the sociology of sport. Utilizing the major frames of reference of the social sciences, the function of sport in contemporary society is examined.
Prereq: Soc 101 and one other Sociology course

courses.label: REC 306
courses.title: Psychodynamics of Leisure Behaviour
paras: Examination of the psychodynamics of popular leisure experiences, e.g. - sport, gambling, fashion, and the like, and their relationship to psychopathology. Examination of the use of leisure experience to resolve emotional conflict and cope with stress.
Prereq: Rec 301, Psych 357

courses.label: REC 307
courses.title: Group Processes in Physical Activity (Kin 354)
paras: An examination of the social influences and group processes which occur within sport teams. Topics include conformity, the influence of onlookers, and co-actors, leadership, group structure, and cohesion. Prereq: 2 term courses in Psychology

courses.label: REC 311
courses.title: School Recreation
paras: An analysis of the relationship between recreation an education with particular emphasis on the sponsoring of community recreation programmes by education authorities including leisure education and co-curriculum activities.
Prereq: Rec 210
Course Descriptions 439 Recreation

courses.label: REC 312
courses.title: Recreation and Community Action
paras: The role of the citizen in recreation systems with regard to social change. Students will examine models for social change which interact with recreation systems and power relationships between citizen’s groups and recreation systems.
Prereq: Rec 210

courses.label: REC 316
courses.title: Principles of Recreation Planning (Plan 344)
paras: An exploration of alternative approaches to the planning of recreation opportunities in urban-centred regions. The demand for and supply of recreation opportunities; standards, models and systems; recreation planning policies and agencies; and selected recreation planning issues.
Prereq: Plan 100 or a full crecit in Geography, or consent of instructor

courses.label: REC 320
courses.title: Evaluation of Recreational Programmes
paras: Evaluation procedures and techniques applicable to recreation programmes are examined in detail. Specification of objectives, development of practical recording procedures and experimental analysis are stressed. Students conduct field evaluations in local community agencies.
Prereq: Rec 270

courses.label: REC 321
courses.title: Selected Topics in Recreation
paras: The study of particular topics pertaining to recreation. Course topics will be announced in advance, but will not be offered on a regular basis. Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: REC 331
courses.title: Outdoor Education in Recreation
paras: The present status of outdoor education in modern society; government functions and policies related to outdoor education services; the planning and administration of outdoor education activities. Current problems.
Prereq: Rec 230

courses.label: REC 332
courses.title: Theory and Practice in Outdoor Recreation
paras: Emphasis on methods and techniques for the selection, development, and implementation of programmes and projects through the utilization of diverse and unique natural settings and environments.
Prereq: Rec 230, 241

courses.label: REC 334
courses.title: Park Management
paras: Basic administrative procedures in park management. Operational techniques are examined together with general policies of acquisition, operation and development.
Prereq: Rec 210, Rec 230 or equivalent

courses.label: REC 361
courses.title: Aging and Leisure
paras: Social parameters of the aging process with particular reference to the Leisure Service Industry. Prereq: Rec 301

courses.label: REC 370
courses.title: Directed Study in Special Topics
paras: For the student who desires to pursue a particular topic in depth through guided independent research and/or reading. A faculty member must approve a student's project prior to registration. May be repeated once in a subsequent term.
Prereq: Faculty approval

courses.label: REC 371
courses.title: Research Designs Applicable to Leisure Studies
paras: An introduction to the methods and techniques of research as applied to leisure studies and services. General consideration will be given to the technical problems involved in various stages of research methodology with emphasis on the logic underlying the research process.
Prereq: Rec 270

courses.label: REC 400
courses.title: Seminar in Recreation and Leisure
paras: An in-depth analysis of the current major issues and trends.
Fourth year Departmental students only

courses.label: REC 402
courses.title: Colloquium on Religion and Leisure
paras: Not offered 1980-81

courses.label: REC 406
courses.title: Comparative Recreational Systems
paras: A study of multi-national recreation systems. Course meets on Campus and in the field in other countries. Full term study over a period of 6-8 weeks. Laboratory fee varies with field observation.

courses.label: REC 410
courses.title: Planning of Recreation Facilities
paras: A course to introduce the students to the planning, design and tayout of recreation areas and facilities. Prereq: Rec 210
Course Descriptions Recreation

courses.label: REC 432
courses.title: Interpretation
paras: Concepts, philosophy and practices relative to understanding the use of the natural environment. Prereq: Rec 332 or consent of the instructor

courses.label: REC 434
courses.title: Advanced Park Management
paras: A study of policies, procedures, and practices relative to the management of natural resources. Emphasis is placed on a systems approach to management as it relates to park management at all levels of government.
Prereq: Rec 334

courses.label: REC 435
courses.title: Recreation Resource Policy
paras: A study of policies, policy development and policy gaps related to recreation resources in Canada. Based on a literature review and discussion of decision-making procedures, roles and tools used in the recreation field; students are required to research real and theoretical situations for seminar presentation.
Prereq: Rec 100 and Rec 230 or consent of instructor

courses.label: REC 470
courses.title: Research Project
paras: An independent research project on an approved topic supervised by a faculty member. Required of all students enrolled in the Honours Recreation Programme.
Rec 470 includes an approved design and completion of the first segment of the paper. Prereq: Rec 270, 371
Rec 471 requires the completion of the project begun in 470.

courses.label: REC 580
courses.title: The Dynamics of Tourism
paras: An examination of the behaviour factors which influence the tourist; the research methodologies employed to examine these factors; and the relationship between tourism and other aspects of leisure behaviour.
Prereq: Rec 302 or equivalent, and a course in Statistics. Open to advanced undergraduate students and graduate students..

courses.title: Modern Study of Jesus
paras: An examination of recent approaches to the study of Jesus of Nazareth to determine his significance for the beginnings of the Christian Church and for modern man.

courses.label: RS 207
courses.title: The Gospel of John
paras: An interpretation of the Fourth Gospel in the light of the situation of the Church at the end of the first century, with an emphasis on the Johannine portrait of Jesus. The letters of John will also be studied. Area 3, Staff

courses.label: RS 209

paras: An examination of the career and thought of Paul as seen in his letters and in the Acts of the Apostles. Area 3, Hubbard

Hinduism

courses.title: Buddhism in India and South-East Asia
paras: An historical survey of the essential doctrines and practices of Buddhism in india and South-East Asia, along with a study of representative texts that illustrate interpretations of the Buddha's teachings that proved to be so significant for the cultures of these areas.
